_comment: Tier-2 for dune::linear_elasticity#0 and #5 — one fixture, one vector space, no scheme (wall time 2 s on a warm cache, 2026-08-06, dune-fem 2.12.0.2). Measured: lagrange(gridView, order=1).dimRange == 1, so the scalar space is the default; space.interpolate([0,0]) on it raises AttributeError; sym(grad(u)) on it raises ValueError 'Symmetric part of tensor with rank != 2 is undefined.' — the UFL-level death the claim describes. With dimRange=2 the same elasticity form builds and carries 2 arguments. Layout: np.array(uh.as_numpy) for the interpolant of (x, 2y) on a 16x16 Q1 vector space is ONE flat array of 578 entries = 17*17 nodes x 2; reshape(-1,2) recovers u_x in [0,1] and u_y in [0,2] exactly, and all 136 entries above 1.0 (which can only be u_y dofs) sit at ODD flat indices. Both facts are needed: under a blocked [all u_x | all u_y] layout reshape(-1,2) would mix the components and both columns would reach 2.0. The half/half misreading differs from the correct one by 1.0 at the worst entry while looking perfectly plausible in range — that is the silent-wrong. Note the 'entries above one are all in the second half' line is printed for completeness and is NOT evidence: u_y = 2y exceeds 1 exactly on the upper half of the domain, which is the second half of this node ordering anyway.
expect_in_output: Symmetric part of tensor with rank != 2 is undefined.
